Gaiskiy GOK DAO Launches New Ore Processing Technology at Russian Mining Facility

Gaiskiy GOK DAO, a major player in Russia’s metals and mining sector, has unveiled a new ore processing technology at its primary facility in Orenburg Oblast. The launch, announced on Thursday, marks a significant step in the company’s ongoing investment in modernization and production efficiency.

According to the company, the new system is designed to improve both throughput and yield in copper concentrate production, while reducing energy consumption by 12 percent compared to previous methods. The facility currently processes over 9 million tonnes of ore annually, and the upgrade is expected to increase output capacity by 8 percent in the coming year.

“Our investment in this advanced technology underlines our commitment to operational excellence and environmental responsibility,” said Ivan Sergeev, General Director of Gaiskiy GOK DAO. “We anticipate not only improved performance but also a reduction in our environmental footprint, which is a priority for our stakeholders and the local community.”

Industry observers have welcomed the move. Elena Morozova, an analyst at the Russian Mining Institute, commented, “Gaiskiy GOK DAO’s adoption of new ore processing technology sets a benchmark for the sector. These upgrades help maintain competitiveness in a challenging market environment.”

The facility employs over 3,500 workers and is a key contributor to the regional economy. The Orenburg Mining Trade Union noted in a statement that ongoing modernization efforts have created additional specialized jobs and training opportunities.

The new technology was developed in collaboration with mineral processing firm EurasiaTech, which provided engineering support throughout the rollout.
